tracks.narration: A half-wave rectifier throws away half the input. Can we keep both halves and still get a one-sided output?
Four diodes wired as a bridge. An AC source on one diagonal, a load on the other. Two diodes will conduct on the positive half, two on the negative.

On the positive half, D1 and D4 conduct. Current flows out the top, through the load, back through the bottom. On the negative half, D2 and D3 take over — but the current through the load still flows top to bottom.
Watch V in trace as a full sinusoid, and V out as the absolute value — every dip flipped above the line, so the ripple frequency is doubled.
Both halves of the wave do useful work — that's why every wall-wart and laptop charger starts with a bridge.
